title: Attribute the three axis hypotheses on one core row (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

A core row kept at distance `ceil(p^{48})` inherits four facts and leaves one bound open:

1. **Row identity, with no gauge.** #4491 gives `R < p^{26} < p^{48} = A`. The section-polynomial row is the global polynomial row.
2. **One section error, under the #4452 gauge.** #4491 gives `||P - H_sec^{-1}||_2 < ε`, with `ε = p^6 exp(-p^2)`. That is `||B - P|| < ε` for `B = H_sec^{-1}`.
3. **Inverse ceiling, under the same gauge.** #4493 proves `U < 9 p^2` for every integer `p ≥ 2`. Under the gauge, the Neumann 1-norm and ∞-norm are strictly below `U`, so `||B|| ≤ 9 p^2`.
4. **Approximant norm, under the same gauge.** #4509 turns that ceiling and that one error into `||P|| < 9 p^2 + ε`. The approximant is the polynomial.
5. **Two-inverse difference.** `||B - C|| < 2 ε` still needs `||C - P|| < ε`. One core row does not supply it.

The integer shadow `|8 - 5| = |8 - 6| + |6 - 5|` separates the pieces. The ideal off-sums `1 - 1/(8 p^2)` stay a hypothesis. This package does not re-prove the radius, the coefficient 9, or the triangle, and it does not claim a new κ. The selected record remains `23/10000`.

This answers the open question of #4509. The next question is whether a second core row supplies the missing section error.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-axis-inheritance`
- [x] Prints `PASS_GAUSSIAN_AXIS_INHERITANCE` and `outcome=completed`
- [ ] Maintainer replay was not run

Base `f9f85c1e4fa1e955ff39f10fca447e3e2a4e4adc`, priority revision 7. Upstream fetched at 2026-10-22T02:57:30Z was that commit, and the pre-submit fetch was unchanged. κ remains `23/10000`.
